findings.title: Race between OnClose disposal and a later refresh leaks dialogs
findings.message: OnClose disposes the control tree and only then calls a.Close(). Between the unlock and Close, a pending refresh can still pass a.Do, reconcile and flushDialogs, creating new external dialog scenes or controls that are never disposed. That leaks native resources after window close.
findings.suggestion: Call a.Close() first so no further Do callbacks are accepted, then take rootMu (which waits for any in-flight refresh) and dispose the tree. Alternatively, set a 'closed' flag under rootMu that refresh checks before reconciling.

finding.title: Programmatic dialog close may be reported as a user dismissal
finding.message: closeDialog sets d.closing for the duration of body.Close() and clears it immediately afterwards. If Cogent delivers the close event to the body's OnClose handler asynchronously, the handler sees closing == false. It then marks the dialog dismissed and calls the model's Dismiss callback even though the model closed it. The handler also sets d.body = nil unconditionally, which could clobber a newly prepared body.
finding.suggestion: Make the OnClose handler identify its own body, for example by comparing `d.body` to the body it was created for and ignoring stale closes. Track programmatic closes per body instead of with a shared flag that is reset right after Close(). Confirm in Cogent whether Close() runs OnClose synchronously.
finding.evidence:
d.closing = true
	tree.MoveToParent(d.host, r.widget)
	d.host.SetScene(r.widget.AsWidget().Scene)
	body.Close()
	d.body = nil
	d.active = false
	d.closing = false
